rules.cwe_name: Use of Potentially Dangerous Function
rules.description: The 'eval' function and the 'Function' constructor execute strings as code. This is dangerous and impedes program analysis and understanding. Consequently, these two functions should not be used.

rules.cwe_name: Uncontrolled Resource Consumption
rules.description: An HTTP request handler that performs expensive operations without restricting the rate at which operations can be carried out is vulnerable to denial-of-service attacks.

rules.cwe_name: Function Call With Incorrect Number of Arguments
rules.description: A function is invoked with extra trailing arguments that are ignored.

rules.cwe_name: Allocation of Resources Without Limits or Throttling
rules.description: Allocating objects or timers with user-controlled sizes or durations can cause resource exhaustion.

rules.cwe_name: Data Processing Errors
rules.description: Legacy category for incorrect handling or transformation of structured data.

rules.cwe_name: Exposure of Sensitive Information to an Unauthorized Actor
rules.description: External links that open in a new tab or window but do not specify link type 'noopener' or 'noreferrer' are a potential security risk.

rules.cwe_name: Expression is Always True
rules.description: Arithmetic comparisons with NaN are useless: nothing is considered to be equal to NaN, not even NaN itself, and similarly nothing is considered greater or less than NaN.

rules.cwe_name: Inclusion of Web Functionality from an Untrusted Source
rules.description: Using a resource from an untrusted or compromised domain makes your code vulnerable to receiving malicious code.

rules.cwe_name: Improper Neutralization of Script-Related HTML Tags in a Web Page (Basic XSS)
rules.description: A string transformer that does not replace or escape all occurrences of a meta-character may be ineffective.

rules.cwe_name: Improper Check for Unusual or Exceptional Conditions
rules.description: Calling a method with a user-controlled name may dispatch to an unexpected target, which could cause an exception.
